source_review.notes: Checked current official Apache Iceberg performance, format, maintenance, configuration, REST catalog, and Puffin documentation; Delta Lake protocol and best-practice documentation; Apache Hudi metadata and technical specifications; Apache Paimon manifest specification; Apache Parquet page-index documentation; and Apache Spark performance guidance. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Product-specific metadata structures are attributed and not assumed interchangeable.

evidence: Reviewed pinned snapshots, manifest lists, manifest/data/delete sets, predicate projection, selected frontiers, metadata bytes, requests, heap, tasks, amplification, prune fractions, and creation/service rates.
Checked set-builder selection, conservative disjointness, count/byte ratios, bounded-memory, and queue-stability expressions with defined domains.
Checked that metadata objects, entries, requests, bytes, selected data, heap, tasks, rates, and latency percentiles remain distinct units.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Planning ratios are scoped diagnostics whose interpretation depends on query class, cache state, snapshot, and metadata cohort.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced 5 total manifests, 2 selected, 440000 indexed entries, 210000 considered entries, 340 total metadata bytes, 160 read bytes, and 52.9% byte reduction.
Recomputed Example 1 entry-count reduction as 1-210000/440000 approximately 52.27%.
Recomputed Exercise 1 as 95% manifest-count, 87.5% manifest-byte, and approximately 93.33% entry-count pruning.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No universal manifest size/count, cache TTL, planner concurrency, heap, compaction, retention, or pruning threshold is prescribed.

evidence: Verified conservative hierarchical pruning preserves matches because unknown or incompatible evidence remains selected.
Verified batching plus backpressure bounds working memory under bounded entry, delete-state, and task-buffer assumptions.
Verified metadata rewrite preserves results when normalized live entry multisets and delete applicability are equal, and verified sustained production above service rate grows backlog.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Fewer objects or successful publication does not by itself prove logical equivalence, bounded planning, or improved selective latency.

evidence: Reviewed empty/no-match/full scans, null/NaN, missing/truncated/incompatible bounds, mixed schema/spec, and data/delete manifest cases.
Reviewed tiny/giant manifests, corrupt checksums, duplicate/missing entries, partial index coverage, concurrent rewrite, branches/tags, unknown commits, and listing lag.
Reviewed cold cache, coalesced misses, thundering herd, cancellation, throttling, driver pressure, spill, tenant fairness, and unavailable indexes.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Uncertain metadata expands the candidate frontier or fails explicitly; it never silently removes matching data or required deletes.

evidence: Traced catalog root, snapshot/reference, manifest list, manifests, file identities, content types, schemas/specs, sequences, metrics, and checksums through planning.
Checked data/delete co-planning, bounded projection/streaming/backpressure, immutable cache keys, exact-input OCC, atomic metadata replacement, and entry equivalence.
Checked reference-aware retention, unknown-commit protection, authoritative reachability, reconciliation, security context, and restore integrity.
invariant_checking.notes: Object-store inventory is used for reconciliation only; the pinned snapshot graph remains membership authority.

evidence: Reviewed hierarchical-pruning, streaming-memory, metadata-rewrite-equivalence, and queue-stability arguments with explicit premises.

Checked counterexamples for unknown-as-empty, current-spec decoding, ignored deletes, unbounded parallelism, name-keyed caches, giant-manifest rewrites, partial-index authority, and age-only orphan deletion.
Checked matched tests span selective/no-match/full scans, evolution, deletes, cold/warm cache, concurrency, throttling, corruption, missing indexes, and retained references.
proof_review.notes: Result correctness, metadata shape, resource bounds, latency, and economic value require separate evidence.

evidence: Audited metadata root, manifest list, manifest, entry, auxiliary index, metadata table, snapshot cache, compaction, expiration, orphan, and reachability terminology.
Confirmed manifest-count, manifest-byte, entry-count, file-count, task-count, and selected-data-byte metrics are distinguished.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Iceberg, Delta Lake, Hudi, Paimon, Parquet, and Spark mechanisms are not presented as identical protocols.

evidence: Reviewed stage latency, total/selected objects and entries, requests/bytes, pruning, cache age/hits, retries/throttles, heap/GC/spill, tasks, data bytes, and maintenance backlog.
Confirmed segmentation by table, predicate/plan class, snapshot/spec, delete cohort, cache state, engine/version, region, tenant, concurrency, and observation horizon.
Confirmed warm latency, fleet median, fewer manifests, high cache hit rate, or low metadata bytes is not mislabeled as bounded tails or correct results.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Sensitive paths, partition values, bounds, predicates, and access patterns require protected or redacted telemetry.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from metadata hierarchy through pruning and resource bounds to compaction, retention, recovery, and measurement. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover frontier math, truncation, evolution, backpressure, manifest sizing, caching, index lag, branches, backlog, and operational diagnosis.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Iceberg/Delta Lake/Hudi/Paimon/Parquet/Spark maintainer, table-format/query-engine/storage/platform/SRE/performance/security specialist, production table operator, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
